Steaming

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
Steam Trains bring back the romance of yesteryear travel - the nostalgia of childhood train trips when many little boys saw the train steam down the tracks and dreamed of being a train driver. Friends of the rail is full of those little boys- except they are grown men who have a passion for Steam locomotives, they call it “Steaming”. Friends of the rail was established 25 years ago and from starting out watching videos and old movies they moved on to restoring old locomotives. One such example is the 19D built by Krupp in Germany in 1937 was rescued from the scrape dealers just in time, and restored lovingly over seven years and is still running today. Another was donated by the Transnet Museum – a rusty old class 24 which they refurbished over 4 years and became their first locomotive they could “Steam” with and start running excursions.
Each locomotive has her own story, and history and this weekend we will be traveling on a 60 year old Diamond Express with passengers seated in old railway coaches dating back to the 1950's - plenty of lovely wood and vinyl seats. The coaches are on loan from The South African Railways who are still the official owners. Friends of the Rail is keeping the history of steam alive in SA instead of sitting in a museum or children’s play park , they are "living" museums. These men and woman love and care for them, maintaining them and making spare parts in their workshop because they are no longer around.


Summary:
Friends of Rail have restored an old station from which their excursions take place. The backbone of their operation is a trip that runs from Hermanstad in Pretoria to Cullinan. The trip runs along the main line in amoungst the current trains which is unusual.

Sadly they have recently been the victim of the metal thieves- on a day trip to Cullinian with a fully laden train they derailed. Fortunately the metal thieves had cut both lines in the same place so instead of tipping over they ground to a rather sudden halt but remained upright. They stole the branch line from Rayton to Cullinan and although they have the railway line, skills and trolleys to do so, because the railway line is owned by the SA Railways so they can’t do the repairs themselves and have to wait for the bureaucratic wheels of SAR to turn. Now they have to bus people for the last 10 kms instead of steaming into the grand old station themselves
It’s a professional operation with all the train drivers taking official drivers licence and being issued with safety certificates which qualify them to take the public on excursions. They are trained by an Ex SA Railways trainer and train driver and have to re-apply for their train licence on a regular basis. These men all have full time jobs or are retired and this is their hobby.
The Cullinan line was built by Paul Kruger to get supplies so they did not have to use the British rail and he escaped to the Eastern Transvaal on this line. Winston Churchill also escaped on this line during the 2nd World War- lots of history on the tracks.

There are many steam train trips around the country but these are all run by corporations and operate as businesses. Friends of the Rail is just a bunch of enthusiast who run the trains out of their own pockets and have fund raising drives. This will be a nostalgic day full of rich characters.

Press Release:


From Pretoria to Cullinan, steam trains are bringing back the romance and nostalgia of yesteryear. “Friends of the rail”, is a group of railway
enthusiasts restoring old locomotives back to their former glory to preserve their place in the history of rail in South Africa. Carte Blanche hops
aboard one of these glorious old steamers

Script:


Link “This is rather a different start to a Sunday morning we are about to go steaming as they call it from this restored station at Hermanstad outside Pretoria all the way to Cullinan and we are being pulled by Jo-Anna who is now in her 70’s and the whistle is about to blow
Nathan “ All aboard
Script: This train is run entirely by an unusual bunch of volunteers who are passionate about keeping steam trains alive. Nathan Berelowitz is the chair Friends of the Rail
Nathan “Because I am a total steam fanatic I had to put these on and I have another on my back but I don’t know if you want to see that
Derek “That is the sign of a real fanatic
Well ye I have got another one on the other side
Nathan “I guess it’s just my childhood dream being realised because from small I wanted to be a train driver which is not too kosher and my wish came true, reach for a dream I got it
Script: But Nathan prefers being a fireman – driving a train is too much responsibility
Derek “Tell us in 30 seconds how this steam engine works
Nathan “ We burn coal in a fire it boils water it generates steam and the driver harnesses the steam on his side of the locomotive and as at home on a pressure cooker you build up the steam pressure to the red mark which is good and if it goes past that it will let steam escape out the top as to check the water level inside here as on you kettle at home you have a water gauge we have 2 of them and I must make sure at all times that I have sufficient water in this locomotive and then we move onto the brakes not like a car where you just put your foot down here you just and up top here as everything needs a bit of lubrication at the best of times we have the locomotive lubricator it feeds oil to the cylinder and the pistons
Script: Les Labuschagne is an engineer but driving steam trains is his obsession, he’s the first privately qualified train driver in South Africa
Les “The fact that the technology is 70, 80 100 years old ……and to be able to take yourself back all those years that what it really is. It’s The art of firing and driving a locomotive in the modern forms of transport on the railways diesels and electrics and so on its pushing a button and pulling a lever with these engines you are physically working everything you have got to know every working part of it and how it should sound and how it shouldn’t sound I absolutely love it it’s something that forms part of you
Link Hooting “ I have seen the sheer enjoyment that Les and Nathan have upfront on the footplate but it takes years and years of hard work and commitment to keep these steam locomotives running
Script: 48 hours before the wheels turn on the tracks there are hours of hard labour all done by what is essentially a bunch of middle aged men. It starts on Friday night when the fire is lit.
Les “there is a lot of steel in the boiler the boiler is full of tubes with flexible and fixed stays so all the steel work has to warm up slowly so you don’t have leaks occurring inside the fire box. Once you have put coal in the fire box and you put a match inside there this big lump of steel comes alive it then comes to life and it is a living machine
Script The entire day on Saturday is spent getting the locomotive ready, and its hard work.
Les “We get the water into the tender have to load coal we have to we have to get everything greased we have to get the locomotive onto the pit it’s got to have road worthy
Script: And before they rescued the fork lift from the scrap heap they loaded 7 tons of coal, bucket by bucket.
Script: Some of these locomotives are over 100 years old and have been lying dormant in this yard for the last 30 years. To the uninformed eye they look like rusting relics, To the Friends of the Rail they filled with history and potential and because they are entirely mechanical they can all work again.
Les “To me they are all just ladies in waiting in the cupboard waiting to be dressed and brought back out onto the line again
Script: And John Dadfords is the man that makes that happen, staring out at 16 on the railways as a fitter he’s still going at 77. He works for Ravos rail in the week and is here on the weekends.
John “ As I said, mad about steam its always been my mission in life to maintain these locomotives keep them going for as long as we can, it’s a feeling a blokes got and fortunately there are a couple of us left
Script: Along with a bunch of old steam men they started Friends of the Rail 27 years ago slowly gathering trains and tools they spent 3 years restoring Jo-Anna which is named after John and his wife.
Robert “ John and I are basically the only ones here in this club that actually got the knowledge umm it looks like the younger generation are not really interested in it we have tried to recruit a lot of people, they come and they go. I took 5 years to learn my trade you can’t learn the guys in a couple of weeks
Script: They scavenged parts from all over the country. Currently they are restoring this large 15CA locomotive because it’s more powerful and economical and will pull more carriages to get their revenue up. They hope to have her running by the end of the year.
John “We have got enough spares to carry on with and we make a lot of stuff too
Robert “What makes me sad in a certain way is I haven’t got many years left
Les “Once the steam fitters go we are sitting with a bit of a problem the drivers and firemen we have got, steam fitters and boiler makers are getting scarce
Script: And they are a special breed
Robert “That locomotive is a living thing it’s alive I have seen where they cut up these locomotives those things moan and groan when they cut them up
Script: There are many groups of Steamers around the country like Umgeni rail in Kwa Zulu and in Ceres rail in the Cape, all trying to keep steam trains on the tracks
Link: These carriages date back to the mid 19 hundreds some of them earlier and they have been lovingly restored to give us a taste of yesteryear. And these day trips are the very life blood of friends of the rail they bring in that much needed cash to keep this mobile museum running
Mom “He’s loving it, he’s mad about trains
Derek” When were you last on a train like this?
Woman “When I was on a young child”
Link “Well unfortunately this is the end of the line when it comes to our trip to Cullinan metal thieves struck a few months ago carting away a couple of hundreds of meters of railway line
Les “We had a very big train on that day carrying a lot of passengers and couldn’t stop in time we came ploughing off the end of the line here the locomotive ended up where that hole is over there
Derek: Do you check the line before you go out
Nathan “Yes the line is checked before the trains but someone could go the morning after they see the car go past and then do their shopping
Les “ Its virtually cut our throat we cannot run these trains and make money off them by only running as far as Rayton because then we have to put our passengers onto buses …the small bit of profit that we make that could go back into the maintenance and continue the projects like the CA for example is being wasted on buses
Script: And it’s not the first time they have been derailed, it happened in 2010 damaging their big locomotive which has been out of action ever since and the metal thieves don’t only take the railway line they also keep busting into the yard and stealing vital pieces of metal off their trains forcing them to strip all the valuable brass and metal and keep it in storage
Link “ So until Transnet replaces that huge gap in the line or allows friends of the rail to get on with the job no steam trains will be pulling in here anytime soon
Script: So while the passengers enjoyed their day in Cullinan we hang out with the crew and forgot their woes
Link “I am sure you have been to many braais in your life but this one is very different it’s a coal shovel braai….. wow that is very hot in there delicious how long does it take to cook, probably round about 4, 5 minutes and you will never taste anything like this in any restaurant We
Derek: Well I look forward to that
Les; This is an old steam locomotive driver fireman tradition. And the tradition is to eat it off the shovel we don’t use plates
Derek “one word for this Smaaklik Smaaklik lekker
